title: How many dryers can a laundry-hanging cell serve when its fold station runs at published robot speeds?
lede: how many dryers can a laundry-hanging cell serve when its fold station runs at published robot speeds? Timed from the SpeedFolding paper (68 to 167 s per garment) rather than an assumed 25 s, one arm and one fold table serve 0.8 to 2.1 dryers instead of 5.1, and with two arms five dryers need 3 to 10 fold tables. Fold times are sourced; every other station time is still assumed.
summary: The hanger-cell model assumed a 25 s fold station and found the arm was the limit (5.1 dryers). Replacing 25 s with the cycle times in Table I of the SpeedFolding paper (Avigal et al. 2022: 68 s for a towel, 88 s fling-to-fold, 117 s t-shirt, 167 s max-value-map baseline, with 80 to 93% fold success) makes the fold table the bottleneck at 98% busy: one arm and one table serve 1.3 dryers at the t-shirt time (0.8 to 2.1 across the rows). With two arms, five dryers need 3 to 10 fold tables depending on the row (5 at 117 s). Prior art at 3 to 6 folds per hour would need more than 40. Hanging every garment instead of folding doubles output at the same tables, but hang-or-fold is a quality choice (hanger-fold), not a throughput one. Fold times and success rates are sourced from one paper measured on one robot and 15 trials per row; the other station times (pick, sense, rail, feeder) are still assumed placeholders from hanger-cell.
